subject: Transportation Systems
title: Instrument Landing Systems
description: A quick win: understand Instrument Landing Systems.

hook.text: Imagine landing a plane when you can't see the runway until 200 feet above the ground. Pilots do it.

buildup.text: An Instrument Landing System sends two radio beams—one for left-right alignment, one for glide slope.

discovery.text: Cockpit instruments show if the plane is above, below, left, or right of the ideal path.

twist.text: Category III ILS allows landing with nearly zero visibility. The autopilot flies the plane to the ground.

climax.text: Without ILS, foggy airports would shut down for hours. Millions of flights depend on these beams.

punchline.text: Two invisible beams guide 300 tons to a safe stop.

quiz.question: What does an Instrument Landing System provide?
options: Left-right and glide slope guidance via radio beams
